channel.title: Chopinly — the blog
channel.description: Writing about practicing the piano, from the people who make Chopinly.

item.title: How to practice piano effectively: a session that actually moves the needle
item.dc:creator: Leif Taylor
item.description: Most piano practice is playing through pieces and hoping. Here is what a session looks like when it is designed to change something: a goal, a small unit, slow and correct, then a test you can't fake.

item.title: How to practice piano with a metronome (without playing like a machine)
item.dc:creator: Leif Taylor
item.description: A metronome is not there to make you play mechanically. It is there to tell you the truth about your rhythm. How to set the tempo, when to use subdivisions, why the off-beat click works, and when to switch it off.

item.title: How long should you practice piano each day? Less than you think, more often than you do
item.dc:creator: Leif Taylor
item.description: Twenty focused minutes beats a distracted hour, and six short days beat one long one. What the research on practice actually says, how to set a daily amount you will keep, and how to know whether it is enough.

item.title: Why keep a piano practice log (and why most of them die in two weeks)
item.dc:creator: Leif Taylor
item.description: A practice journal is the single most effective tool a self-taught pianist can adopt, and almost nobody keeps one. What a log is actually for, what to write in it, and how to make one that does not need filling in.

item.title: Ear training for pianists: why the keys let you skip it, and how to stop skipping it
item.dc:creator: Leif Taylor
item.description: Pianists can play music they cannot hear. That is the instrument's gift and its trap. A practical route into ear training at the piano: what to drill, in what order, and how ten minutes a day at the instrument rewires the ear to the hands.

item.title: Sight singing for pianists: the ten-minute habit that fixes your sight reading
item.dc:creator: Leif Taylor
item.description: Pianists avoid singing, and their sight reading suffers for it. Why singing a line before you play it is the fastest route to inner hearing, how to start when you don't think you can sing, and a routine that fits before breakfast.

item.title: How to memorize piano music so it doesn't fall apart on stage
item.dc:creator: Leif Taylor
item.description: Playing from memory is not the same as having memorized. Four kinds of memory, why finger memory alone fails under pressure, and a method for building the others — starting points, analysis, hearing, and the tests that tell you it is really there.

item.title: Stuck on a plateau? What to change when piano practice stops working
item.dc:creator: Leif Taylor
item.description: Every pianist hits a stretch where the hours go in and nothing comes out. Plateaus are usually a sign that the practice has stopped being practice. How to diagnose which kind you are on, and the specific changes that get things moving again.
